business_problem: Salesforce needed its observability platform to scale far beyond the limits of on-premises data centers so it could onboard more internal services, improve availability, and reduce the operational burden of growing telemetry infrastructure.
solution_summary: Salesforce migrated its internal observability platform from on-premises data centers to AWS to remove capacity bottlenecks and support company growth. Using AWS MAP for acceleration, the team redesigned the platform around fully managed services including Amazon RDS and Amazon EKS so it could scale telemetry ingestion, alert evaluation, dashboarding, and querying without waiting on first-party hardware. The platform now ingests around two billion metrics per minute and more than 1 PB of logs, evaluates nearly 250,000 alerts every minute, and serves more than 20,000 dashboards in near real time. Managed cloud infrastructure also reduces operational toil because many underlying database and platform issues are absorbed by AWS services, allowing engineering teams to add capacity in a day and spend more time improving architecture and product innovation.

solution_components.name: Amazon RDS
solution_components.role: Handles managed database responsibilities inside the migrated observability platform.

solution_components.name: Amazon EKS
solution_components.role: Runs containerized observability workloads at the scale Salesforce requires.

data_flow: Telemetry metrics and logs from Salesforce services are ingested into the AWS-based observability platform, where Amazon EKS-hosted workloads and supporting managed data services power alerting, dashboards, and near-real-time queries for internal engineers.
business_outcome: By 2022 Salesforce had migrated over 95 percent of the observability platform to AWS, scaled to around two billion metrics per minute and more than 1 PB of logs, reached 99.99 percent availability for alerting, added capacity in 1 day instead of days or weeks, and freed 10–15 percent of team time for innovation.
